item.title: Springs in Series and in Parallel Supporting a Block
item.stimulus:
Two ideal springs have spring constants k₁ = 200 N/m and k₂ = 300 N/m. Use g = 10 m/s².

Arrangement 1: Spring 1 hangs from a fixed ceiling hook, spring 2 hangs from the bottom of spring 1, and a 3.0 kg block hangs from the bottom of spring 2. The block hangs at rest.

Arrangement 2: Both springs hang side by side from the ceiling, and their lower ends are attached to a light horizontal bar from which the same 3.0 kg block hangs. The bar stays horizontal, so both springs stretch by the same amount, and the block hangs at rest.

parts.prompt: For Arrangement 1, calculate the equivalent spring constant of the two springs and the total stretch of the two-spring combination.

criteria.evidence: Response adds the reciprocals of the two spring constants and obtains 120 N/m.
criteria.fix: For springs connected end to end, add the reciprocals of the spring constants, then take the reciprocal of that sum.

criteria.text: Total stretch = mg/k_eq = (30 N)/(120 N/m) = 0.25 m.
criteria.evidence: Response divides the 30 N spring force (equal to the block's weight) by its own k_eq and obtains 0.25 m.
criteria.fix: At rest, the spring force equals the weight; divide that force by the equivalent spring constant to find the total stretch.

parts.prompt: For Arrangement 1, determine how much each spring stretches, and explain why the two springs exert forces of the same magnitude.

criteria.text: Both ideal (massless) springs carry the full 30 N, so spring 1 stretches (30 N)/(200 N/m) = 0.15 m and spring 2 stretches (30 N)/(300 N/m) = 0.10 m.
criteria.evidence: Response states that each massless spring transmits the same 30 N force and gives stretches of 0.15 m and 0.10 m, which add to the total from part (a).
criteria.fix: In a chain of massless springs each spring carries the whole load; divide that force by each individual spring constant.

parts.prompt: For Arrangement 2, calculate the equivalent spring constant and the distance each spring stretches.

criteria.text: k_eq = k₁ + k₂ = 200 N/m + 300 N/m = 500 N/m.
criteria.evidence: Response adds the two spring constants to obtain 500 N/m.
criteria.fix: For springs side by side that stretch by the same amount, add the spring constants directly.

criteria.text: Each spring stretches (30 N)/(500 N/m) = 0.060 m.
criteria.evidence: Response divides the 30 N load by its own parallel k_eq and obtains 0.060 m.
criteria.fix: Divide the total load by the parallel equivalent spring constant; each spring then stretches by that same amount.

item.model_answer:
(a) Springs connected end to end are in series:
1/k_eq = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂ = 1/200 + 1/300 = 5/600, so k_eq = 120 N/m.
At rest, the spring force on the block balances its weight, mg = (3.0 kg)(10 m/s²) = 30 N.
Total stretch = (30 N)/(120 N/m) = 0.25 m.

(b) Spring 2 pulls up on the block with 30 N. Because spring 2 is ideal and has no mass, spring 1 must pull up on spring 2 with the same 30 N, so both springs exert 30 N.
Spring 1: Δx₁ = (30 N)/(200 N/m) = 0.15 m.
Spring 2: Δx₂ = (30 N)/(300 N/m) = 0.10 m.
Check: 0.15 m + 0.10 m = 0.25 m, matching part (a).

(c) Side by side and stretching equally, the springs are in parallel:
k_eq = k₁ + k₂ = 200 N/m + 300 N/m = 500 N/m.
Each spring stretches Δx = (30 N)/(500 N/m) = 0.060 m.
Check: spring 1 exerts (200)(0.060) = 12 N and spring 2 exerts (300)(0.060) = 18 N, which total 30 N.
item.verification_python:
from fractions import Fraction as Fr
k1, k2 = Fr(200), Fr(300)
W = Fr(3)*Fr(10)
assert W == 30
inv = 1/k1 + 1/k2
assert inv == Fr(5,600)
kser = 1/inv
assert kser == 120
assert kser < min(k1, k2)
x_tot = W/kser
assert x_tot == Fr(1,4)
x1, x2 = W/k1, W/k2
assert x1 == Fr(15,100) and x2 == Fr(10,100)
assert x1 + x2 == x_tot
kpar = k1 + k2
assert kpar == 500
xp = W/kpar
assert xp == Fr(6,100)
assert k1*xp == 12 and k2*xp == 18 and k1*xp + k2*xp == W
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')
